extracted.intended_audience: short story writers and authors looking for contests to enter
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for submitting short stories (including flash fiction, novellas, and novel openings) to a variety of literary contests, covering eligibility, formats, word/page limits, fees, judging, and publication/prize outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to contest-specific word/page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each contest enforces explicit length limits (words or pages) that submissions must meet (e.g., Reedsy Literary Prize: '2,000 to 5,000 words'; Globe Soup: 'up to 8,000 words'; Fiction Factory: 'up to 1000 words'; Dream Quest One: 'short stories (up to 5 pages)'; Jerboa Lit 250: '250 words'; Ethos Literacy: 'exactly 100 words').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the precise limit for the contest you enter; contests vary from exact-word micro-contests (100, 250 words) to multi-thousand-word short stories and multi-page limits. Some contests distinguish flash vs short story categories with different caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and unpublished status requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Many contests require submissions to be original and unpublished (e.g., MoonLit Getaway: 'All submissions must be original and unpublished.'; Seán Ó Faoláin: 'open to original, unpublished, and unbroadcast short stories in English'; Lorian Hemingway: 'original, unpublished stories').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a contest specifies 'original' and/or 'unpublished' the story must not have been previously published or broadcast; check whether reprints/simultaneous publication are permitted per contest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme or prompt adherence when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests require submissions in response to a specific prompt or theme (e.g., Reedsy Prompts: weekly prompts; Reedsy Literary Prize: 'in response to one prompt'; Jerboa Lit 250: participants write 'based on a prompt given 48 hours prior'; Hope Prize: 'focused on original stories of hope').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write to the supplied prompt or theme where required — failing to follow the prompt can disqualify entries or make them ineligible for judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre and category eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests define allowed genres and categories (many list multiple genres such as Crime, Fantasy, Horror, Romance, Science Fiction, Short Story, Flash Fiction, etc.). Some contests are multi-genre; others are genre-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter only in the category/genre the contest accepts; check exclusions (some contests exclude certain age categories or content types).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific exclusions (children's/YA, erotic, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests explicitly exclude or restrict certain subgenres or age-targeted works (e.g., Fiction Factory: 'excluding children's and young adult fiction'; Paul Cave Prize: 'excluding erotic work').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify content exclusions before entering; inappropriate category entries can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fee & free-entry options
rubrics_metrics.description: Most contests list an entry fee (e.g., Reedsy Prompts: $5; Best Indie Book Award: $65; many others vary), while some contests are free to enter (e.g., BBC National Short Story Award: $0; Not Quite Write Prize: $0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay the specified entry fee where required and check for different fees by category or number of submissions. Confirm refund/cancellation policies if provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and timely submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each contest provides a firm deadline by which entries must be received (examples throughout the list include dates such as 'May 31, 2026', 'December 31, 2026', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit before the stated deadline in the contest's required submission system; late entries are generally ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility based on prior publication or author status
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests restrict entrants by publication history or publication route (e.g., Best Indie Book Award: 'entries are limited to indie published books'; Drue Heinz: requires authors to have 'published a book-length collection or at least three short stories/novellas in commercial magazines'; Emerging Author Dagger: for 'writers who have never had a publishing contract for a full-length novel').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check author/publication eligibility before entering; some contests target emerging/unpublished writers while others accept or require published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and broadcast restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain contests require submissions in a specific language and not previously broadcast (e.g., Seán Ó Faoláin: 'original, unpublished, and unbroadcast short stories in English').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure story language matches contest requirement and that the work has not been broadcast if prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests differ on whether simultaneous submissions (submitting the same work to multiple contests/publications) are allowed: some explicitly allow or 'encourage' them (e.g., Berkeley Fiction Review 'encourages simultaneous submissions'); others permit simultaneous or unspecified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowed, promptly notify contests/publications if a simultaneous submission is accepted elsewhere; if disallowed, withdraw other entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests use varied judging setups: blind judging (e.g., Not Quite Write: 'Judging is blind'), guest judges and editorial panels (e.g., Reedsy Literary Prize: 'longlisted stories reviewed by our guest judge Jon Michael Darga'), and panels of judges or national writers (e.g., Drue Heinz judged 'anonymously by national writers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow any submission instructions required for anonymous judging (remove identifying information) and note whether stories will be read by editors, guest judges, or panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission material requirements beyond the story
rubrics_metrics.description: Some competitions require additional materials with submissions (e.g., Emerging Author Dagger: 'submission of a crime novel opening (max. 3,000 words) and a synopsis (max. 1,500 words)'; Mary McCarthy Prize: full-length manuscript).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare required supplementary documents (synopsis, manuscript, sample chapters) to the specified length and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of author rights / ownership statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contest descriptions note that entrants retain ownership of their work (e.g., Globe Soup: 'Participants retain ownership of their work').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review contest terms for rights granted on acceptance/publication; retain copies and confirm whether publication is exclusive or non-exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication & anthology inclusion terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Many contests offer publication or anthology inclusion for winners/finalists (e.g., Reedsy Prompts winners 'may also be included in a future issue of Reedsy’s literary magazine, Prompted'; The Plaza: 'Top 10 entries published in anthology'; Seán Ó Faoláin: 'Publication in Southword').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether publication is part of the prize, whether payment is provided for publication, and any rights transfer or licensing associated with publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize structure and non-monetary benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests list monetary top prizes and additional benefits such as feedback, mentorship, agent feedback, membership subscriptions, trophies, or festival passes (examples: Reedsy Literary Prize top prize $1,500 + agent feedback; Writer's Digest top prize $5,000 + subscriptions; Queen Mary Wasafiri Prize includes mentoring and publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note both cash and career-development prizes and any conditions attached (e.g., feedback provided to the winner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category entry and multi-category submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests have multiple categories (e.g., Writer's Digest with multiple categories; Storytrade Book Awards with many categories) and may allow or require separate entries per category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the correct category for each entry and check whether multiple entries across categories are permitted and whether separate fees apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age or residency restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain contests require entrants to meet age or residency criteria (e.g., The Bedford Competition: 'open to anyone over 17 years'; Hope Prize: 'open to writers aged 18 and over' and entries accepted in English).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm age and residency eligibility before submitting; proof may be required for winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific content or format exceptions (previously published allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: A few contests explicitly allow previously published work or simultaneous submissions (e.g., The Lascaux Prize 'accepts both previously published and unpublished stories, allowing simultaneous submissions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a contest allows previously published material, check whether there are restrictions (e.g., only certain types of prior publication allowed) and whether payment differs for reprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions or special requirements for children's/young adult categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests explicitly exclude children's and YA fiction from certain categories (e.g., Fiction Factory 'excluding children's and young adult fiction'), while other contests include children's categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to category labels and exclusions so submissions are entered into appropriate divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript-length vs. short-form distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain prizes target full-length manuscripts or novel openings rather than standalone short stories (e.g., Morton and McCarthy Prizes: 'full-length manuscript of literary fiction'; Emerging Author Dagger: 'crime novel opening (max. 3,000 words) and a synopsis').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether the contest targets single stories, collections, openings/sample chapters, or full manuscripts and prepare the submission accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized contest aims (charitable, emerging voices, indie focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests have mission-based eligibility (e.g., Do WHA(TS) Write! raises funds for Tourette Canada; Queen Mary Wasafiri Prize 'celebrates emerging voices' and supports writers without published book-length works; Best Indie Book Award recognizes indie published books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether your background or publication route aligns with the contest's mission; mission-focused contests may prioritize certain voices or publishing paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification/public announcement and runner-up publishing opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Many contests not only name winners but publish shortlisted or runner-up entries (e.g., BBC National Short Story Award: shortlisted stories; Plaza Short Story Prize: 'Top 10 entries published in anthology'; Berkeley Fiction Review: 'Publication in the journal for top finalists').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand publication opportunities for finalists/runners-up and any expectations for promotional activities or anthology contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical contest logistics (registration/registration fee, deadlines per round)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests require registration/registration fee and have multiple rounds or registration deadlines (e.g., The Writers Cypher: 'first year, three-round virtual creative writing competition' and requires a 'first-round entry and $20 registration fee by December 30th').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track registration deadlines, round schedules, and fees for multi-round competitions to ensure continued eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content suitability and adult-only content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests that publish or accept erotic content often require entrants to be adults (e.g., Not Quite Write Prize for FLESH Fiction: 'open to adults worldwide').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting adult content, verify age verification requirements and whether the contest has additional consent or labeling rules.
